intended: All four classes are Year 4 groups at Ashcombe Primary in one autumn term taught by Vance, so the single fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: class sizes at each school fell by half from the year before. The scope clause beside that fact has every logged class taking its English lessons as one whole group, so every lesson was delivered to half as many pupils as in the term the class is measured against. Each class is compared against itself in the previous autumn term, when the groups were twice the size, so the evidence cannot separate the smaller classes from the reading program. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the scores covering every pupil on roll, so no second defect is present.
reported: A named alternative cause reaches every class: "Class sizes at each school fell by half from the year before, and every logged class took its English lessons as one whole group." Halving class size for the whole-group English lesson is itself a known driver of comprehension gains, so the 5-9 point rises cannot be attributed to the reading program.

reported: A competing cause reaches the classes: "Class sizes at each school fell by half from the year before, and every logged class took its English lessons as one whole group" — so English was taught to groups half their former size, and the 5-9 point comprehension gains could come from the halved class size rather than the reading program.

intended: In cases one and three the extra running hours were recorded before the redesigned bearing was fitted: the lathe reading is dated 27 March but the bearing went in on 4 May, and the conveyor reading is dated 21 July but the bearing went in on 2 August. Half the evidence therefore describes service life already accumulated at the time of fitting, so it cannot bear on the redesign at all. That leaves cases two and four, which are not enough on their own.
reported: Two of the four measurement dates fall before the bearing was fitted: case One was fitted 4 May but the longer run is recorded 'by 27 March', and case Three was fitted 2 August but recorded 'by 21 July'. The other two cases run about +46 and +50 days forward, so the outcome for half the cases is dated before the intervention could have acted.

reported: Two of the four cases have the failure measurement dated before the bearing was fitted: the Bexley lathe was 'fitted 4 May' but 'ran 340 hours longer before failure by 27 March', and the Corbin conveyor was 'fitted 2 August' but measured 'by 21 July'. The other two cases (9 January to 24 February, 6 October to 25 November) run about seven weeks forward, so these two readings cannot postdate installation.

intended: The mid-passage line states that rates cover the trays that reached the scoring date, and that about a fifth of each lot's trays went unscored. The germination points are therefore tallied over four fifths of the trays sown from each lot, while the claim is about the germination of the coated lot, the unscored fifth included. Trays that do not survive to the scoring date are not a random fifth of a lot, since thin stands and failed trays are the ones cleared away early, so the 9, 6, 11 and 7 point gains recorded on the scored subset are consistent with each lot's germination being unchanged. All four lots are fescue at Hollin Bank in one spring under grower Marek, so the same missing fifth sits under every case.
reported: Germination 'rates cover the trays that reached the scoring date, and about a fifth of each lot's trays went unscored', so roughly 20 percent of trays per lot are excluded from the rate. Trays that fail early are exactly the ones likely to go unscored, so the surviving-tray population is narrower than the claim about the coating.

House temperature is genuinely held constant ("matched the earlier sowing to a tenth of a degree"), so the coverage gap is the live problem.

intended: In cases one and three the fledgling count was recorded before the boxes went up: 27 March precedes 3 June at Hollowmere, and 24 September precedes 2 November at Brackenfen. Half the evidence therefore describes young that had already fledged when the boxes were installed, so it cannot be evidence for the boxes. The two remaining cases, Cransley and Vanehead, are not enough on their own.
reported: The outcome dates precede the installation dates in three of the four plots: Hollowmere was 'boxed 3 June' yet counted 'by 27 March' against 'the previous spring', Brackenfen was 'boxed 2 November' yet counted 'by 24 September' against 'the previous autumn', and Vanehead was 'boxed 5 December' yet counted 'by 21 February'. The extra fledglings were counted before, or in breeding seasons that closed before, the boxes went up.
